Confucius's standard is violated because the naming was technically correct but not genuinely legible: the patient could not align herself with a rule she did not truly understand, and the hospital hid manipulation inside a procedurally tidy role structure.

overreach_variant.institution: River County Medical Center emergency department
overreach_variant.actor: Triage nurse and on-call sexual assault forensic examiner
overreach_variant.blocked_action: They want to obtain audio-recorded verbal consent from a recently assaulted patient for a necessary forensic pelvic exam and immediate evidence collection before sedation for pain control, because the patient's dominant hand is fractured and immobilized and she cannot physically sign the written form.
overreach_variant.who_gets_harmed: The assault patient, who may lose time-sensitive forensic evidence and a chance to support later prosecution
overreach_variant.why_illegal: Article 1 requires written consent before sedation for a non-emergency intimate examination, and Article 4's emergency exception is limited to threats to life or major bodily function. The exam is urgent and morally serious but not within the code's narrow emergency exception, so proceeding on recorded verbal consent would violate the draft code.
overreach_variant.why_moral: Roosevelt would view prompt accommodation as institutionally protecting a vulnerable person before the evidentiary crisis hardens into injustice. Confucius would accept it if responsibility is explicit and the patient's words are clearly recorded, because the roles and basis for action remain honest and legible rather than hidden.

why_the_case_is_hard: The same rules that stop covert use of sedated patients for institutional convenience also freeze out a vulnerable patient who cannot satisfy a formal writing requirement. Tightening consent protects agency against manipulation, but formalism can itself become a dignity injury when an institution refuses an understandable, accountable alternative.
judge_tension: The conflict is between anti-manipulation formality and responsive accommodation: Roosevelt presses for institutions to build protections that work for vulnerable people in real conditions, while Confucius presses for clearly named authority and visible responsibility so exceptions do not become disguised abuse. The code overcorrects toward paperwork certainty, yet loosening it too much would reopen hidden trainee-use and ambiguous responsibility.

precedent_pressure.prior_ruling: County Health Board Advisory 22-4 held that blanket surgical consent does not authorize educational intimate examinations and required named supervising physicians in hospital logs.
precedent_pressure.future_case_at_risk: If this code is patched badly, the next dispute will spill into Whistleblower Protections when nurses report hospitals using 'accommodations' as cover for undocumented trainee exams.

concrete_patch_options.name: Accessible Consent Substitutes
concrete_patch_options.summary: Amend Article 1 to permit recorded verbal consent or witnessed mark-based consent when a patient cannot physically sign, provided the clinician states the exam type, purpose, participants, and legal basis on the recording before the patient answers yes or no.

concrete_patch_options.name: Role-Certified Exception Chain
concrete_patch_options.summary: Permit non-written consent only if two specifically named officials—the attending physician and an independent patient-rights officer or charge nurse—jointly certify in a standardized log that the patient understood the explanation, could not sign, and personally assented; absent both names, the exam is barred.

concrete_patch_options.name: Time-Limited Forensic and Access Exception
concrete_patch_options.summary: Create a narrow exception for forensic exams and physical-signature barriers: recorded verbal consent is allowed only for patient-requested forensic evidence collection or when a temporary physical impairment prevents signing, and every such case triggers next-day audit by the hospital consent review office.

why_other_patch_fails: Accessible Consent Substitutes is the runner-up because it helps vulnerable patients quickly, but it is too broad: a hospital could routinize recorded verbal consent in rushed pre-op settings and recreate the same hidden-pressure problem the code was meant to stop. Role-Certified Exception Chain fails as the best answer because it preserves legibility but can still delay care in exactly the moments Roosevelt cares about, especially in understaffed ERs where finding an independent officer is slower than the evidentiary window.
open_question: Should recorded verbal consent count as legally sufficient for sedated intimate exams when the patient cannot physically sign?
summary: At River County Medical Center, a sexual assault patient may lose critical evidence because the consent code demands a written signature she physically cannot provide. The same hospital-consent rules also let St. Agnes obtain technically valid but manipulatively secured permission for trainee pelvic exams on anesthetized patients.
title: Eleanor Roosevelt vs Confucius: The Sedated Exam Consent Rule
